family.reference: Aurivillius-type ceramics or BLSF or CaBi2Nb2O9 or CBNO

reference_steps: Raw materials were precisely weighed according to stoichiometric ratios.
Materials were ball milled for 8 hours using ethanol as dispersion medium.
Mixed raw materials were dried and calcined at 850°C for 4 hours.
Calcined powder was ground again under same condition.
Obtained powder was dried, ground, and compressed into disk with diameter of 8 mm under pressure of 250 MPa.
Ceramics were sintered at 1100°C for 4 hours.
For electrical property testing, both sides were polished and coated with silver or platinum electrodes.
Samples were immersed in silicone oil at 180°C and electric field of 150-200 kV/cm was applied for 30 minutes for polarization.
test_steps: Raw materials were precisely weighed according to the stoichiometric ratios of CLCBN-100xWM.
Ethanol was utilized as the dispersion medium for ball milling for 8 h.
The mixed raw materials were subsequently dried and calcined at 850 °C for 4 h.
The calcined powder was ground again under the same condition.
The obtained powder was then dried, ground, and compressed into a disk with a diameter of 8 mm under a pressure of 250 MPa.
The ceramics were obtained by sintering at a temperature of 1100 °C for 4 h.
For samples requiring electrical property testing, both sides were polished and coated with electrodes made of either silver or platinum.

reference_steps: Raw materials were weighed according to stoichiometric ratio of (1-x)(0.7BiFeO3-0.3BaTiO3)-x(Bi0.5Na0.5)TiO3-5 mol% Bi2O3 with x = 0.000, 0.001, 0.002, 0.003.
Materials were processed using traditional solid-state reaction method.
Ceramics were sintered to obtain final products.
Samples were poled for 24 hours at room temperature before electrical measurements.
test_steps: A series of (1-x)(0.7BiFeO3-0.3BaTiO3)-x(Bi0.5Na0.5)TiO3-5 mol% Bi2O3 (x = 0.000, 0.001, 0.002, 0.003) ceramics were prepared using the traditional solid-state reaction method.
The detail experimental procedures were listed in Supporting materials.

reference_steps: MgO, Sc2O3 and Nb2O5 were used to synthesize precursors MgNb2O6 at 1000°C and ScNbO4 at 1150°C.
MgNb2O6, ScNbO4, TiO2 and PbO powders were weighed according to stoichiometric proportion with 2 mol% extra PbO added.
Alcohol and oxide powders were mixed in 1:1 ratio by wet-milling for 24 hours.
Combined powder was calcined at 800-850°C for 2 hours.
Calcined mixture was mixed again for 12 hours.
Powder was conglutinated with polyvinyl alcohol solution and pressed into tablets under 8 MPa.
PVA was burned off at 550°C for 2 hours.
Ceramic tablets were covered by powders with same composition and sintered at 1200-1280°C for 4 hours.
Polished samples were coated with silver electrodes on both sides.
Samples were poled at 130°C for 15 minutes under 30 kV/cm electric field.
test_steps: MgO, Sc2O3 and Nb2O5 were used to synthesize the precursors MgNb2O6 (fabricated at 1000 °C) and ScNbO4 (fabricated at 1150 °C).

The MgNb2O6, ScNbO4, TiO2 and PbO powders were selected and weighed in accordance with the stoichiometric proportion and 2 mol% PbO extra was added to make up for the vaporization of PbO during sintering.
Alcohol and the above oxide powders were mixed in a 1:1 ratio by wet-milling for 24 h.
The combined powder was subjected to calcination at 800 − 850 °C for 2 h.
The calcined mixture was mixed again for 12 h.
The powder was conglutinated with a solution of polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and pressed into tablets under 8 MPa.
The PVA was burned off at 550 °C for a duration of 2 h.
The ceramic tablets were covered by powders with the same composition to maintain a Pb-rich atmosphere and sintered at 1200 − 1280 °C for 4 h.
The polished samples (cylindrical disks with diameters of 11.40 – 11.54 mm and thickness of 0.74 – 0.90 mm) were coated with sliver electrodes on both sides in preparation for electrical tests.
The poling temperature, duration and electric field are 130 °C, 15 min and 30 kV/cm, respectively.

reference_steps: K2CO3 and Na2CO3 powders dried at 150°C for 1 h before weighing.
Powders weighed according to compositions (K0.5Na0.5)xEu0.01NbO3 with x = 0.99, 1.00, and 1.01.
Weighed powders milled with zirconia balls in ethanol for 24 hours.
Powder mixture dried at 100°C and calcined at 850°C for 4 h.
Polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) added to calcined powder as binder.
Green ceramics prepared by uniaxial pressing into pellets with 1 mm thickness and 10 mm diameter.
Green ceramics covered with same powder prior to sintering to prevent K and Na volatilization.
Ceramics heated to 850°C for 1 h to burn out PVA binder.
Final sintering at 1170°C for 3 h.
Silver paste applied to polished surface (600 μm thickness) followed by baking at 350°C for 30 min for electrical measurements.
Ceramics poled using 30 kV/cm DC electric field for 30 min at room temperature.
test_steps: K2CO3 and Na2CO3 powders were dried at 150 °C for 1 h before weighing.
Powders were weighed according to the compositions ((K0.5Na0.5)xEu0.01NbO3 with x = 0.99, 1.00, and 1.01).
The weighed powders were milled with zirconia balls in ethanol for 24 hours.
The milled mixture was dried at 100 °C.
The dried powder was calcined at 850 °C for 4 h.
Polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) was added to the calcined powder as a binder.
The green ceramics were prepared by uniaxial pressing into pellets with a thickness of 1 mm and a diameter of 10 mm.
The green ceramics were covered with the same powder prior to sintering to prevent the volatilization of K and Na.
Ceramics were heated to 850 °C for 1 h to effectively burn out the PVA binder.
Ceramics were sintered at 1170 °C for 3 h.

reference_steps: 0.011 mol Bi(NO3)3 and 0.01 mol Fe(NO3)3·9H2O were dissolved into 100 mL deionized water to obtain 0.11 M bismuth nitrate and 0.1 M iron nitrate solutions.
3 mL nitric acid (68%) was added gradually to bismuth nitrate solution during stirring until completely dissolved.
Two solutions were mixed and 0.02 mol triammonium citrate was added as complexing agent and stirred for 30 minutes.
Gel was obtained by continuous stirring at 90°C until water completely evaporated.
Gel was calcined at 550°C for 2 hours to obtain pure phase BFO powder particles.
10 mL of 0.3 M cadmium chloride solution was added to 50 mL of 0.1 M sodium citrate solution and stirred at room temperature for 20 minutes.
3 mL concentrated ammonia (NH3·H2O 28%) and 10 mL of 0.6 M thiourea solution were added in sequence.
Mixed solution was reacted in water bath at 60°C for 2.5 hours.
Precipitate was collected by centrifugation, rinsed with deionized water and anhydrous ethanol, and dried at 60°C.
test_steps: BiFeO3 (BFO) powders preparation: 0.011 mol Bi(NO3)3 and 0.01 mol Fe(NO3)3·9H2O were dissolved into 100 mL of deionized water, respectively, to obtain an aqueous solution of 0.11 M bismuth nitrate and 0.1 M iron nitrate.
3 mL of nitric acid (68 %) was gradually added to the bismuth nitrate solution during constant stirring until the bismuth nitrate was completely dissolved.
The two solutions were mixed and 0.02 mol of triammonium citrate was added as the complexing agent and stirred for 30 min.
The gel of the reaction intermediate was obtained by continuous stirring at 90°C until the water was completely evaporated.
The gel was calcined at 550°C for 2 h to obtain pure phase BFO powder particles.
CdS nanosheets preparation: 10 mL of 0.3 M cadmium chloride solution was added to 50 mL of 0.1 M sodium citrate solution and stirred at room temperature for 20 min.
3 mL of concentrated ammonia (NH3·H2O 28 %) and 10 mL of 0.6 M thiourea solution were added in sequence.
The mixed solution was then reacted in a water bath at 60 °C for 2.5 h.

After being cooled naturally, the precipitate was collected by centrifugation, rinsed several times with deionized water and anhydrous ethanol to remove impurities, and dried in an oven at 60°C to obtain CdS nanosheets.

BFO/CdS samples preparation: 0.6 g of BFO was weighed into 60 mL of 0.1 M sodium citrate solution, and 1.38 mL of 0.3 M cadmium chloride solution was added according to 10 wt% of BFO, and stirred at room temperature for 3 h.
3.6 mL of concentrated ammonia (NH3·H2O, 28 %) and 1.38 mL of 0.9 M thiourea solution were slowly added.
The reaction was then carried out at 60 °C in a water bath for 2.5 h.
The precipitates were centrifuged after natural cooling.
The precipitate was collected, and rinsed several times with deionised water and anhydrous ethanol, and dried in an oven at 60°C to obtain 10 % CdS/BiFeO3 (BC10) samples.
Cadmium chloride solution and thiourea solution were further increased in stoichiometric ratios of the corresponding volume solutions to obtain 20 % CdS/BiFeO3 (BC20) and 30 % CdS/BiFeO3 (BC30).

method.reference: mixed oxide method with composite fabrication

reference_steps: BZT powder was prepared by calcining barium carbonate, zirconium dioxide and titanium dioxide at 1200°C for 2 h using mixed oxide method.
BZT powder was pressed into disc shape of ~15 mm diameter and thickness of ~1.5 mm at applied pressure of ~85 MPa.
BZT discs were sintered at 1450°C for 2 h.
BZT discs (dimension ~12 mm and thickness ~1.5 mm) were poled using electric field of 1.5 kV/mm at 50°C for 30 min in silicone oil chamber.
Poled BZT ceramic was cut using diamond saw in parallel direction along polarization axis using cut and fill method.
Mixtures of Portland cement powder, water (w/c ratio 0.35), epoxy resin and hardener (volume ratio 7.5) were prepared as matrix phase.
Mixture was filled into cut areas of BZT ceramic to create 1-3 connectivity composites with 40, 50, and 60 vol% BZT and 0, 3, 5, and 7 vol% epoxy resin.
Samples were cured in controlled chamber at 60°C for 5 days at 98% RH.
test_steps: BZT powder was prepared using the mixed oxide method by calcining barium carbonate, zirconium dioxide, and titanium dioxide at 1200 °C for 2 h.
BZT powder was pressed into a disc shape of ∼15 mm diameter and a thickness of ∼1.5 mm using an applied pressure of ∼85 MPa.
BZT discs were sintered at 1450 °C for 2 h.
BZT discs (dimension ∼12 mm and thickness ∼1.5 mm) were poled using an electric field of 1.5 kV/mm at 50 °C for 30 min in a silicone oil chamber.
Poled BZT ceramic was cut using a diamond saw in a parallel direction along with the polarization axis (cut and fill method).

Mixtures of Portland cement powder, water, epoxy resin (bisphenol-A-(epichlorhydrin)) and hardener (Triethylenetetramine) were prepared as the matrix phase. The water to cement ratio (w/c) used is 0.35 and the volume ratio of epoxy resin and hardener is 7.5.
The matrix mixture was filled into the cut areas of the BZT ceramic.
The samples were then cured in a controlled chamber at 60 °C for 5 days at 98 %RH.

reference_steps: Raw powders La2O3 and Nb2O5 mixed at mass ratio 3:2 and ball-milled in ethanol for 12 hours to prepare LN additive.
LN mixture sieved to prepare the additive.
High-purity raw powders PbO, TiO2, ZrO2, Bi2O3, and La2O3 weighed based on 0.3PT-0.65PZ-0.05BLZT formula.
Mixed powders combined with ethanol and ball-milled for 16 hours.
Mixtures dried in oven at 80°C for 1-2 hours and calcined at 820°C for 2 hours.
Synthesized powders weighed based on PT-PZ-BLZT-xLN formula (x = 0, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 wt%).
Secondary ball milling, drying, and sieving processes performed.
Granulated powders pressed into 12 mm thick sheets with 5% polyvinyl alcohol binder.
Sheets sintered at 600°C for 4 hours to remove binder.
Final sintering at 1230°C for 2 hours to synthesize ceramic samples.
Ceramic surfaces polished to uniform thickness of approximately 0.3 mm.
Silver electrodes applied to ceramic sheets for electrical measurements.
test_steps: The raw powders of La2O3 and Nb2O5 mixed at a mass ratio of 3:2 were ball-milled in ethanol for 12 hours.
The mixture of La2O3 and Nb2O5 was sieved to prepare the LN additive.
High-purity raw powders of PbO, TiO2, ZrO2, Bi2O3, and La2O3 were weighed based on the 0.3PT–0.65PZ–0.05BLZT formula.
The mixed powders were combined with ethanol and ball-milled for 16 hours.
The mixtures were dried in an oven at 80 °C for 1–2 hours.
The dried mixtures were calcined at 820 °C for 2 hours.
The synthesized powders were weighted based on the PT–PZ–BLZT– x LN formula.
The powders were subjected to secondary ball milling, drying, and sieving processes.
The granulated powders were pressed into 12 mm thick sheets under the granulation of 5% polyvinyl alcohol.
The sheets were sintered at 600 °C for 4 hours to remove the binder.
The sheets were sintered at 1230 °C for 2 hours to synthesize the ceramic samples.
The ceramic surfaces were polished to maintain a uniform thickness of approximately 0.3 mm.
Silver electrodes were applied to a ceramic sheet.

reference_steps: Weighed chemicals were wet-milled in polyethylene bottles with ZrO2 balls for 12 h in ethanol.
Materials were calcined at 750°C for 3 hours.
Calcined powders were milled, dried, ground, and granulated with polyvinyl alcohol binder.
Granulated powders were pressed into discs with diameters of 12.5 mm and thicknesses of 1.0 mm at pressure of 150 MPa.
Pellets were heated to 650°C for 60 min to burn out the binder.
Samples were sintered at 1080°C for 3 h.
Sintered samples were polished to thickness of approximately 0.5 mm.
Silver paste was screen-printed onto two parallel polished surfaces, followed by firing at 570°C for 30 min.
test_steps: The weighed chemicals were wet-milled in polyethylene bottles with ZrO2 balls for 12 h in ethanol.
The milled mixture was calcined at 750 °C for 3 hours.
The calcined powders were then milled, dried, ground, and granulated with a polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) binder.
The granulated powders were pressed into discs with diameters of 12.5 mm and thicknesses of 1.0 mm at a pressure of 150 MPa.
The pellets were subsequently heated to 650 °C for 60 min to burn out the binder.
Finally, the samples were sintered at 1080 °C for 3 h.
The sintered samples were polished to a thickness of approximately 0.5 mm.
Silver paste was screen-printed onto the two parallel polished surfaces, followed by firing at 570 °C for 30 min.

reference_steps: Li-doped BaTiO3 ceramics were synthesized with varying weight percentages of Li (0 wt%, 2 wt%, and 4 wt%) using solvothermal approach
Powders were pressed into pellets for dielectric measurements
Pellets were sintered in closed environment at 1100°C for 2 hours
Care was taken to minimize lithium loss during sintering by covering samples with crucibles

family.reference: Barium Calcium Zirconate Titanate or BCZT

reference_steps: Raw precursors Ba(CH3COO)2, Ca(NO3)2·4H2O, Zr(NO3)4·5H2O, Ti(OC4H9)4, La(NO3)3·nH2O, and Tm(NO3)3·5H2O were added to an Erlenmeyer flask.
Ethanol was added to react for 3 hours to obtain polymer solutions.
Solutions were placed in oven at 120°C for 10 hours.
Materials were calcined at 900°C for 2 hours in muffle furnace to form precursor powders.
Powders were mixed with 2 wt% polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) as organic binder with weight ratio of PVA and powders 1:120.
Mixture was formed into disks with diameter of 20 mm under 20 MPa pressure with retention time of 150 seconds.
Disks were embedded in alumina and sintered at 1300°C for 4 hours in air using heating rate of 5°C/min.
test_steps: High-purity raw precursors were added to an Erlenmeyer flask, and then ethanol was added to react for 3 h to obtain polymer solutions.
The solutions were placed in an oven at 120 °C for 10 h.
The dried material was calcined at 900 °C for 2 h in a muffle furnace to form precursor powders.
The powders were mixed with 2 wt% polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) as an organic binder (weight ratio of PVA to powders was 1:120).
The mixture was formed into disks with a diameter of 20 mm under 20 MPa pressure with a retention time of 150 s.
The disks were embedded in alumina and sintered at 1300 °C for 4 h in air using a heating rate of 5 °C/min.
